and content
    ObjectivesThe learning objectives are: i) Understanding the organization of computer networks, including heterogeneous networks of networks such as the Internet, or the Internet of Things, ii) understanding the Internet structure and how standard problems are solved in that context, iii) being able to analyze simple network protocols, and iv) being able to independently study literature concerning computer networks.
 

    ContentThe OSI model; notions: protocol, connection, application, service; network topology, network components and physical media; overview of relevant services; the link layer; the network layer and routing; the Internet protocol; naming; addressing; the transport layer: TCP, UDP; reliability and multiplexing; performance characteristics and quality of service

    Remarkstarts in 2024    Short promotional description of the courseThe course is organized as an introduction into networks. We will discuss why we need networks, how networks function and what the main issues are. The course offers a dual approach: theoretical exploration network theory, involving study and reporting on contemporary literature; and practical application through hands-on lab sessions, providing tangible experience.
